THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the Insurance Company has challenged the judgment and award dated 01.12.2016 passed in M.V.C.No.519/2023 by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and J.M.F.C., Chikkamagaluru in awarding a compensation of Rs.21,51,432/- with 6% interest p.a.
2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 09.06.2013 at about 07:00 am, the husband of 1st petitioner, father of 2nd petitioner by name Denis D'souza, the deceased, while riding his Yamaha motor vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-18/R-9127 along with 1st petitioner as a pillion rider, in front of Classic NC:
2023:KHC:37643 Hotel Road at Koppa Bus Stand, a private bus bearing Reg.No.KA-16/B-813 came from the opposite direction hit against the motor cycle killing the deceased at the spot and injuring the 1st petitioner.
The 1st petitioner as an injured and both the petitioners being the dependants of the deceased, have approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation.
Claim was opposed by the respondents.
The Tribunal after taking the common evidence in both the petitions, by impugned judgment awarded Rs.21,51,432/- on account of death of the deceased.

Aggrieved by the same, the Insurance Company has filed this appeal on the grounds that the 1st petitioner is employed as a Teacher and she is not dependant of the deceased and she is entitled only loss of estate.

The deceased was left with only 2 years of service and application of multiplier on the basis of the age of the deceased is not proper and deduction towards personal expenses ought to be 50% instead of 1/3rd.

Heard the arguments of Sri. A.N. Krishnaswamy, learned counsel for the Insurance Company and Sri. Dinesh. M. Bhat, learned counsel for respondents No.1 and 2.
5.
It is the contention of learned counsel for the Insurance Company that the 1st petitioner though is a wife of the deceased, she is also employed as a Teacher, she is not dependant of the deceased.
Petitioner No.2 is a married daughter, she is also not a dependant of the deceased.
The deceased was aged 58 years, '9' multiplier is applied by the Tribunal instead of applying the split multiplier.
Since the deceased left behind the 1st petitioner, 50% has to be deducted towards personal expenses and sought for modification of the impugned judgment and award.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that the deceased was working as a Deputy Range Forest Officer (D.R.F.O.) NC: 2023:KHC:37643 on the date of accident, he was drawing a salary of Rs.30,000/- per month.

The principles of split multiplier is not applicable to the case and there is no scope for 50% deduction towards personal expenses as the petitioner herself is aged 59 years, she is also going to retire in a year and the deceased would retire in 2 years.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier and assessed the compensation and he supported the impugned judgment.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8. There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident, death of the deceased on account of the accident and entitlement of the petitioners to claim compensation.

Three grounds urged by the Insurance Company are:
NC: 2023:KHC:37643 (i) The 1st petitioner is not a dependant as she herself is a Teacher, earning independent income and she is entitled only for compensation towards loss of estate.
(ii) The deceased was aged 58 years, he would retire in two years if he was alive.

The applicable multiplier is '9' for the age of the deceased, he was left with only two years of service, hence his salary cannot be considered for assessment of income and it shall be reduced to 50% of the salary.
(iii) Since the 2nd petitioner is a married daughter, for a sole dependant, 50% has to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased.
9. The material on record did point out that the 1st petitioner is aged 59 years, she is left with only one year of service.
On retirement, she is a dependant on her husband.
The deceased was aged 58 years, after two years, he is also the dependant NC: 2023:KHC:37643 on his wife.

Hence, the 1st petitioner and the deceased are inter-dependants and therefore, I do not find any force in the argument of learned counsel for the Insurance Company that the 1st petitioner is not entitled for compensation under loss of dependency.
10. There is no dispute that the 2nd petitioner is a married daughter.
She is aged just 31 years.
I do not find any force in the argument of learned counsel for the Insurance Company that 50% has to be deducted towards personal expenses as the deceased having wife and daughter to be maintained.
Hence, the Tribunal has rightly deducted 1/3rd towards personal expenses.

11. As regarding applicability of split multiplier is concerned, this Court in The Branch Manager, The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. -Vs.-
The Regional Manager vs Emilda Pinto on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134996710/
3 NC: 2023:KHC:37643 Mallamma and others1 (in which I am also one of the member) has held that under what circumstances, split multiplier is applicable.

entities.text: Branch Manager, The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: Here in this case, the deceased was working as a D.R.F.O.
There is no evidence on record that post-retirement, the deceased will get such an avocation which will earn him any income more than the salary.
Being a D.R.F.O., there is no scope for any employment post-retirement which creates him additional income.
For 58 years, applicable multiplier is '9'.
Since the deceased was left with only 2 years of service, his income will be reduced to 50% after 2 years.
Hence, the facts are identical to the case referred above and it is a case for application of split multiplier.
12. In a case of this nature, principles of assessment of compensation is settled by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd.

(2023) 3 KCCR 242.
NC: 2023:KHC:37643 -vs- Pranay Sethi and Others2 and Sarla Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation and Another3.

entities.text: Sarla Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ex.P9 is the salary certificate pertains to the deceased.
He was drawing a salary of Rs.29,256/-, it could be considered for calculation of loss of dependency.
Future prospects of 15% is applicable for the age between 50 to 60 years as the deceased was in a permanent employment.
Hence, compensation has to be calculated by applying the above principles and applying the concept of split multiplier i.e., '2' multiplier for the full salary, '7' multiplier for the pension.
Total loss of dependency comes to Rs.14,80,380/-.

Under conventional heads, Rs.20,000/- each is assessed towards loss of consortium to wife and loss of love and affection to the daughter, Rs.10,000/- each is assessed towards funeral expenses and loss of estate.
Then, the total compensation comes to Rs.15,40,380/- as against Rs.21,51,432/- assessed by the Tribunal, thereby reduction of Rs.6,11,052/-.
Accordingly, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed in part.
ii) Impugned judgment is modified.
iii) Petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,40,380/- as against Rs.21,51,432/-, thereby reduction of Rs.6,11,052/-.

iv) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation with interest of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within eight weeks from The Regional Manager vs Emilda Pinto on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134996710/
